answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to earn reputation through verifiable work history recorded on a shared ledger, like a sonnet whose lines only make sense in sequence. New accounts start with no trust and must complete small paid tasks whose outputs are checked by established peers. A fake identity cannot echo the same proof twice, because each attestation is bound to a unique key and timestamp; creating thousands of sock puppets would cost more in saffron-priced compute and fees than any reward they could extract, making the attack uneconomical.
